arxiv-2112-03373.title: Proton structure functions at low x : the Fractal distributions
arxiv-2112-03373.creator: Samira Shoeibi Mohsenabadi 1,2 ID, Shahin Atashbar Tehrani 2 ID, Fatemeh Taghavi-Shahri 1 ID
arxiv-2112-03373.description: Abstract This paper presents a method for extracting the Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) at small momentum fractions x and at the next-to-leading order (NLO) accuracy in perturbative quantum chromodynamics. It turns out that the PDFs can be described by the ”Fractal” or self-similar distributions at low x below x < 0.01 x<0.01 .

arxiv-2305-04666.title: Power Distribution Grid Enhancement via Online Feedback Optimization
arxiv-2305-04666.creator: Jonas G. Matt, Lukas Ortmann, Saverio Bolognani, Florian Dörfler
arxiv-2305-04666.description: Abstract The rise in residential photovoltaics and other distributed energy sources poses unprecedented challenges for the operation of power distribution grids. The high active power infeed of such sources during peak production is a stress test that distribution grids have usually not been exposed to in the past.

arxiv-2312-15974.title: Analysing Rescaling, Discretization, and Linearization in RNNs for Neural System Modelling
arxiv-2312-15974.creator: Mariano Caruso, Cecilia Jarne
arxiv-2312-15974.description: Abstract Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are widely used for modelling neural activity, yet the mathematical interplay of core procedures used to analyze them?temporal rescaling, discretization, and linearization?remains undercharacterized. This study establishes the conditions under which these procedures commute, enabling flexible application in computational neuroscience.

arxiv-2402-05948.title: DE 3 -BERT: Distance-Enhanced Early Exiting for BERT based on Prototypical Networks Thanks: This work was supported in part by the National Key Research and Development Program of China under Grant 2022YFB3104700, in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant 61976158, Gran
arxiv-2402-05948.creator: Jianing He, Qi Zhang, Weiping Ding, Senior Member, IEEE, Duoqian Miao, Jun Zhao
arxiv-2402-05948.description: Abstract Early exiting has demonstrated its effectiveness in accelerating the inference of pre-trained language models like BERT by dynamically adjusting the number of layers executed. However, most existing early exiting methods only consider local information from an individual test sample to determine their exiting indicators, failing to leverage the global information offered by sample population.

arxiv-2407-18914.title: Floating No More: Object-Ground Reconstruction from a Single Image
arxiv-2407-18914.creator: Yunze Man, Yichen Sheng, Jianming Zhang, Liang-Yan Gui, Yu-Xiong Wang
arxiv-2407-18914.description: Abstract Recent advancements in 3D object reconstruction from single images have primarily focused on improving the accuracy of object shapes. Yet, these techniques often fail to accurately capture the inter-relation between the object, ground, and camera. As a result, the reconstructed objects often appear floating or tilted when placed on flat surfaces.

pmc-10573328.title: Optimization of Antibacterial Activity and Biosafety through Ultrashort Peptide/Cyclodextrin Inclusion Complexes
pmc-10573328.creator: Hang Liu, Lin Wang, Chen Yao, Klaus Brandenburg
pmc-10573328.description: Engineered ultrashort peptides, serving as an alternative to natural antimicrobial peptides, offer benefits of simple and modifiable structures, as well as ease of assembly. Achieving excellent antibacterial performance and favorable biocompatibility through structural optimization remains essential for further applications. In this study, we assembled lipoic acid (LA)–modified tripeptide RWR (LA–RWR) with β–cyclodextrin (β–CD) to form nano–inclusion complexes.

pmc-11545838.title: Honokiol and Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide Improve Exercise Endurance in Pulmonary Hypertensive Rats Through Increasing SIRT3 Function in Skeletal Muscle
pmc-11545838.creator: Min Li, Brittany Alexandre McKeon, Sue Gu, Ram Raj Prasad, Hui Zhang, Sushil Kumar, Suzette Riddle, David C Irwin, Kurt R Stenmark, Lukasz Buldak
pmc-11545838.description: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) significantly impairs exercise capacity and the quality of life in patients, which is influenced by dysfunctions in multiple organ systems, including the right ventricle, lungs, and skeletal muscles. Recent research has identified metabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial dysfunction as contributing factors to reduced exercise tolerance in PH patients.

pmc-11863107.title: Associations between cerebellar development and autistic traits during adolescence: a population-based cohort study
pmc-11863107.creator: C. Morimoto, S. Koike
pmc-11863107.description: IntroductionBrain maturation is associated with adolescent socio-cognitive development. The lateral posterior region of the cerebellum plays a critical role in higher cognitive processes, and deviations of this region are associated with autism-related behaviors. Hence, it is plausible that developmental changes in this region of the cerebellum during adolescence are different along a variation in autistic traits.

pmc-12594893.title: CERS6 promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma proliferation by increasing the stability of RPN1
pmc-12594893.creator: Wenjing Chen, Yuxin Zhai, Xiaoxiao Yang, Weizhe Zhang, Dan Gao, Xiaokun Zhao, Nannan Zhao, Yuhan Zhang, Qiang Yuan, Zhiying Zhao, Qiong Wu, Yifei Xie, Jimin Zhao, Zigang Dong, Kangdong Liu, Yanan Jiang
pmc-12594893.description: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is associated with poor prognosis because it is typically diagnosed at a moderate or advanced stage. Investigating the precise molecular mechanism of ESCC pathogenesis is essential for developing new therapeutic strategies. In this study, we demonstrated that ceramide synthase 6 (CERS6) was overexpressed and correlated with a worse prognosis in ESCC.

pmc-13096219.title: Longitudinal changes in cardiorespiratory fitness and risk of depressive and anxiety disorders in a nationwide cohort of 7 million participants
pmc-13096219.creator: Jin-Hyun Park, Seokjin Kong, Yohwan Lim, Yunhwan Oh, Porwarat Chawanid, Batuhan Gökbulut, Ju-Wan Kim, Sun Jae Park, Hye Jun Kim, Sangwook Cheon, Eun Seok Kang, Seohui Jang, Jeongin Lee, Minjeong Kang, Taeho Kwak, Yihyun Kim, Jihun Song, Jaewon Khil, Su Kyoung Lee, Jae-Min Kim, Seogsong Jeong, Hwamin
pmc-13096219.description: While baseline cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) is inversely associated with mental health disorders, the association of longitudinal CRF changes on depression and anxiety risk remains unclear in large-scale populations. This study investigated the association between changes in estimated CRF (eCRF) and subsequent risk of depressive and anxiety disorders in Korean adults.
